sector_strength.bottom: bottom third conflicts with a bullish view
sector_strength.several: majority of the matching indices (supports vs conflicts); a tie is neutral

targets.conservative: the nearest 20-session resistance (support for a short) at least min_resistance_atr x ATR beyond the entry, else 1 x ATR(14)

combinations.short_call_strike: the call wall (largest call open interest) when it lies above the at-the-money strike, else the first listed strike at or beyond spot + one expected move
combinations.long_put_strike: the listed out-of-the-money put strike nearest the stop (the scanner's stop, else the chart engine's ATR stop)
combinations.future: the futures contract that expires on the options expiry (a synthetic call needs matching expiries)
combinations.shares: lots x lot size shares, at the last close; if the stock is already held, the shares leg is that position priced at the last close
combinations.reward_risk: reward = P&L at the gate scenario level, risk = loss if the price reaches the stop (both from the payoff calculation); a long put or a short call changes that loss, so the ratio is not comparable with an unhedged cash idea: read max loss and capital at risk beside it. When the premium received covers the loss at the stop, the ratio is undefined and the gate is not applied.
combinations.sizing: lots = floor(risk budget / loss per lot at the stop (the cash stop distance x lot size when the premium covers it)), capped by the allocation cap on the deployed value per lot (shares or futures notional plus the net premium)

sizing.formula: units = the most whole lots with units x risk per unit + estimated round-trip costs at the stop (the desk cost card) <= risk budget, capped by floor(capital x max allocation % / entry value per unit); for an option structure the risk per unit is already its worst net loss

chartink.ranking: Chartink-only ideas follow the AI scanner's ideas; they are ranked by the number of enabled bullish Chartink scans that listed the stock, then by 20-session traded value. That is a count of the user's own scans, not a probability and not a score.
chartink.gates: the same eligibility gates as scanner stocks (the scan snapshot: price, 20-session traded value, reference data, series EQ or BE, not an ETF, price band, not at its band limit, traded value of at least the liquidity gate); a stock that is not in the snapshot cannot be tested and is excluded
chartink.evidence: technical.chartink_scans: a bullish-tagged scan hit supports a bullish view and conflicts with a bearish one, a bearish-tagged hit the reverse; hits of both tags are neutral; no hit is neutral; no dashboard, a stale or failed refresh is unavailable
chartink.cash_rule: A stock the scanner lists in no bucket, with at least one enabled bullish Chartink hit, gets a cash candidate whose stop, targets and sizing come from the chart engine's ATR rule (ATR_2X_STOP); the same reward : risk, liquidity and event gates as every other candidate apply
chartink.levels_label: rule-based levels; the scan is the user's Chartink scan, not validated

chartink_picks.label: evidence score — not a probability
chartink_picks.rule: Each Chartink stock that passes the scan-snapshot eligibility gates is scored on scan confluence, trend (EMA), momentum (MACD, 20-day change, RSI), relative volume, liquidity, F&O open-interest build-up (F&O stocks), fundamentals quality, event risk (results inside the horizon), distance from its 52-week extremes and ATR risk. A figure that could not be read earns nothing and is listed as unavailable. Thin or conflicting evidence, a score under the minimum, or a strategy plan that says wait or no trade, is Wait / No trade and the stock is not a candidate. Strategies come from the Strategy Builder's plan; options are defined risk only and nothing is sent to a broker.

Collar (shares + long put + short call) is for a stock with event or gap risk, and here there is none (no results date inside the horizon and the risk class is not high): insurance would be a cost without a reason.

Futures + protective put (synthetic long call) is for a stock with event or gap risk, and here there is none (no results date inside the horizon and the risk class is not high): insurance would be a cost without a reason. The plain long future carries the idea.

failure_conditions: Stale data: a price older than 4 calendar days, or an F&O chain older than the last completed session, means wait.
Liquidity: average traded value below 10 Cr a day, or a leg with no open interest or volume, means no trade.
Event risk: results inside the horizon (the plan avoids them).
Reward : risk below 1.5 (at the nearest resistance when one caps the move, else at the base level) means no trade.
Failed confirmation: for a long idea, a close back below the trigger or the invalidation level cancels it.
Breakout continuation (long): invalid on a close beyond 1160 (the scanner's stop (1160): 1.5 x ATR(14) below 1195 (ATR 23.33)).
Long futures: build-up with cash confirmation: invalid on a close beyond 1150 (the put wall (FnoStrategies rule 2)).
Long call: invalid on a close beyond 1150 (the put wall (FnoStrategies rule 2)).
Bull call spread (debit): invalid on a close beyond 1150 (the put wall (FnoStrategies rule 2)).
Covered call (shares + short call): invalid on a close beyond 1160 (the scanner's stop (1160)).
